China Holds 5-Year Loan Prime Rate at 3.50% in September, Signaling Policy Steadiness
body: China kept its 5-year Loan Prime Rate (LPR) unchanged at 3.50% in September 2026, matching the level set in August 2026. The decision, confirmed in data updated on 20 September 2026, indicates continued stability in a key benchmark that heavily influences mortgage costs and long-term corporate borrowing rates. By maintaining the 5-year LPR at 3.50% for a second consecutive month, policymakers are signaling a steady approach to long-term funding conditions. With no shift in the rate between August and September, markets may interpret the move as an effort to balance support for the property sector and broader credit demand with concerns about financial stability and longer-term risk. Investors and analysts will now watch upcoming economic releases and policy signals for clues on whether Beijing will lean toward further easing or keep long-term rates anchored at current levels for an extended period. The unchanged 5-year LPR suggests that, for now, authorities are opting for continuity over additional stimulus in the long-term lending market.
